messages.subject: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
Hi all.

I have several plots representing the evolution of different quantities (with very different scales - %, 0-1 and 0-2000) measured at the same times along a day cycle. I need to organize them in a vertical strip, so that their x-axis are aligned. I use grid.layout for this, but I have the problem that they have different widths of the y-axis viewport (because the tick-mark labels have different maximum lengths).
My question is how can I make the plots such that the width of the y-axis viewport is the same. I've been looking, but found no way to access the width of the viewports.

Thanks,
Pedro

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
Hi,

It's probably easier if you can use facet_grid of facet_wrap with a
dummy conditioning variable: this way, ggplot2 does the work for you.

If you have use grid.layout, maybe you can use this trick to retrieve
the dimension of the label viewport,

qplot(1,1000)
grid.ls(grob=F, viewp=T)

seekViewport("ylabel")
a = grid.rect(gp=gpar(col="blue"))
convertUnit(grobWidth(a), "mm")

seekViewport("axis_v-3-1")
a = grid.rect(gp=gpar(col="red"))
convertUnit(grobWidth(a), "mm")

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
> a) If I use the facetting options, how can I use different scales for
> each of the plots, considering that I want to define the limits and
> axis breaks manually?
>

Hi,

To have different scales, use the scales="free_y" parameter of
facet_wrap. However, you can't set the limits and breaks manually in
each facet. see this post:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/6455332126d33bbe/bc561433658c0789?lnk=gst&q=xavier#bc561433658c0789

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
Well, you can use a trick to set the limits for each facet: subset the
data beforehand to shorten a given limit or add dummy data if you want
to extend the range,

d1 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10, f=factor("a", levels=letters[1:2]))
d2 <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=1e3*1:10, f=factor("b", levels=letters[1:2]))
d <- rbind(d1, d2)

## create dummy data to extend the range of both panels
## independently

lim1 <- data.frame(x=c(1, 10), y=c(0, 15), f=factor("a"))
lim2 <- data.frame(x=c(1, 10), y=c(0, 25e3), f=factor("b"))
lims <- rbind(lim1, lim2)

set_lims <- function(...)
geom_blank(data=lims, map=aes(x, y))

p <- ggplot() + facet_grid(f~., scales="free")+
geom_point(data=d1, map=aes(x, y)) +
geom_path(data=d2, map=aes(x, y)) +
set_lims()

p

However I can't get facet_grid or facet_wrap to free both x and y
scales. I don't know why.


HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
Below is a minimal example (hopefully it could be simplified a little bit),

p1 <- qplot(1,1000) + ylab("double\nline")
p2 <- qplot(1,1)

g1 <- ggplotGrob(p1)
g2 <- ggplotGrob(p2)

## retrieve the relevant components and
## strip their viewport (needed to calculate the sizes before drawing)
ytit1 <- editGrob(getGrob(g1,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL)
ylab1 <- editGrob(getGrob(g1,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL)
ytit2 <- editGrob(getGrob(g2,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL)
ylab2 <- editGrob(getGrob(g2,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL)


gl <- grid.layout(nrow=2)
vp <- viewport(layout=gl)
pushViewport(vp)
## calculate the sizes
width2 <- grobWidth(ytit2) + grobWidth(ylab2)
width1 <- grobWidth(ytit1) + grobWidth(ylab1)
width.diff <- width2-width1

pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=1))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(1, "npc"), width=unit(1, "npc"), just="right"))
grid.draw(g1)
upViewport(2)
pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=2))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(1, "npc"), width=unit(1, "npc")+
width.diff, just="right"))
grid.draw(g2)
upViewport(2)

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Multiple plots with same size of y-axis viewport
parts:
p3 <- qplot(1,100)

align.plots <- function(...){

dots <- list(...)
dots <- lapply(dots, ggplotGrob)
ytitles <- lapply(dots, function(.g)
editGrob(getGrob(.g,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL))
ylabels <- lapply(dots, function(.g)
editGrob(getGrob(.g,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE), vp=NULL))
## one should also deal with the legends...

gl <- grid.layout(nrow=length(dots))
vp <- viewport(layout=gl)
pushViewport(vp)
widths <- mapply(`+`, e1=lapply(ytitles, grobWidth),
e2= lapply(ylabels, grobWidth), SIMPLIFY=F)
widths.max <- max(do.call(unit.c, widths))

for(ii in seq_along(dots)){
pushViewport(viewport(layout.pos.row=ii))
pushViewport(viewport(x=unit(1, "npc"), width=unit(1, "npc") -
widths.max + widths[[ii]], just="right"))
grid.draw(dots[[ii]])
upViewport(2)
}
}

align.plots(p1, p2, p3)


Best,

baptiste
